newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BRAZIL AND ITALY GIVE COMMAND PERFORMANCE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-BRAZIL AND ITALY GIVE COMMAND PERFORMANCE.

text.p: World champions Brazil and Italy, World Cup winners seven times between them, served up a feast of football as they drew 3-3 in a brilliant Tournoi de France clash of giants on Sunday.
No other result would have been fair or fully reflected the total commitment of both sides to winning and playing good attacking football which augurs well for next year's World Cup in France.
It also handed the tournament to England, who have beaten both Italy and France, with one match each to go in the World Cup dress rehearsal.
Brazil coach Mario Zagallo said: "This evening's match was a spectacle apart, especially in the second half."
The Brazilians came from 3-1 down to score two superb goals through twin strikers Ronaldo and Romario in the final 19 minutes.
The 1994 World Cup veteran, taking a square ball from his 20-year-old partner, jinked his way through the defence to score Brazil's superb 84th-minute equaliser.
Ronaldo, put through by left back Roberto Carlos, sent Italy's goalkeeper Gianluca Pagliuca the wrong way after rounding the defenders and finding the net with a low shot to the left.
Italy coach Cesare Maldini said: "This was a very beautiful match. I thank my players because they gave everything. I also congratulate the Brazilian team because they showed they are a great side."

The Italians had earlier looked set to reverse their defeat in the 1994 World Cup final, the last and only goalless meeting between the two sides in 11 encounters and which was settled in Brazil's favour on penalties.
The result left the two big guns of international football equal at five wins each with two draws and a goals tally of 19-19.
Brazil looked like they were going to pay dearly for a sloppy start when Alessandro Del Piero put the more purposeful Italians ahead in the seventh minute.

Midfielder Demetrio Albertini, one of four survivors of the 1994 World Cup final in the Italian side, began a move down the right by feeding young Juventus striker Christian Vieri, whose fine cross to the far post was headed home by Del Piero.

At the other end, the Brazilian attack was struggling to break free of the tight marking by the Italians. Christian Panucci was on Romario and Fabio Cannavaro keeping a tight rein on Ronaldo, but midfielder Dino Baggio was also doubling up as a custodian of playmaker Leonardo.

The match developed into a balanced, high level contest between two contrasting styles even though the Brazilians went further behind after 24 minutes when a free-kick on the right by Albertini was deflected past Taffarel by Aldair for the first of two own goals in the match.

The other own goal brought Brazil back into the contest 12 minutes later when a bullet shot from the left by Roberto Carlos was turned past Pagliuca, who was also in Italy's side in the 1994 Los Angeles showdown, by Attilio Lombardo.

It was an unfortunate moment for the balding Juventus winger who had done well thus far to keep the Real Madrid left back busy in defence. When it came to defending against Brazil's deadly shooter he put a foot badly wrong.
The action went from end to end almost unrelentingly with both midfields working hard and inventively.

Sao Paulo's young midfielder Denilson, the only change in the Brazil side that drew 1-1 with hosts France on Tuesday, came more and more into the game as he gained in confidence in his fourth international.
Denilson forced Pagliuca into a brilliant diving save after a fine solo run on the left six minutes into the second half, then shot just wide of the far post three minutes later.
He also put Romario through with a brilliant back heel, but the Flamengo striker was edged out by the defence.
Italy should have had a penalty in the 55th minute when Celio Silva upended Del Piero as the Juventus forward turned the Cornithians defender on the left of the box.

Seven minutes later Italy did get a penalty when substitute Filippo Inzaghi, just two minutes into his first international, was brought down by Aldair. Del Piero put the ball to Taffarel's right and Italy 3-1 up.

Brazil, who lost 4-2 to Norway in Oslo five days before the Tournoi started and have now conceded eight goals in their last three internationals, stormed back and in between their second and third goals Roberto Carlos hit the bar with another of his thunderbolts.
Substitute Flavio Conceicao and captain Dunga, on whose steadying influence Brazil constructed their fightback, also had shots from outside the box saved by Pagliuca.

Inzaghi might have put Italy beyond reach when he was put free on the right of the Italian attack with little more than 10 minutes remaining but Taffarel turned his shot from a tight angle over the bar.
Instead it was left to the resurrected Romario to have the last word.
